::: {#rem-codes-pcp}
#### Codes in the PCP theorem

The PCP theorem says that every statement in NP
has a proof that a randomized verifier can check
by reading a constant number of its bits
and using only $O(\log n)$ random bits,
where $n$ is the length of the statement.
@arora2009computational [chapter 11] prove a weaker version,
in which the verifier uses polynomially many random bits,
by writing the proof in the [Hadamard code](#def-hadamard-code).
The verifier then tests a few random positions of the encoded proof,
in the spirit of @thm-hadamard-local-decoding,
instead of reading all of it.
They prove the full theorem in chapter 22.

:::
